newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran rejects Turk protest over anti-Israel rally.
newsitem.headline: Iran rejects Turk protest over anti-Israel rally.

text.p: Iran rejected on Wednesday a Turkish protest over the participation of Tehran's ambassador in an anti-Israel rally in Turkey, calling it a move instigated by "Zionists", the official news agency IRNA said.
It quoted Deputy Foreign Minister Alaeddin Boroujerdi as saying the Turkish Foreign Ministry's summoning of ambassador Mohammad Reza Baqeri was "unacceptable".

Boroujerdi said the summoning on Monday over the envoy's role in the protests organised by a town council run by Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party was a "move by the Zionists against Iran", IRNA said.

The rally on Friday was linked to Jerusalem Day, the last Friday of the Islamic holy month of Ramadan which was declared a day of protest against Israel by the late Iranian leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.
"He (Boroujerdi) said that what the Iranian ambassador to Turkey did is usually done by every Iranian diplomat in the world," IRNA said.

The event upset Turkey's secularist elite. A speech at the event by the Welfare Party mayor of Ankara's Sincan district was blasted by Turkish media as a call for the implementation of Islamic sharia law. He was arrested on Wednesday for questioning about the rally.

The mayor and the Iranian ambassador spoke on a stage draped with banners of Fathi Shqaqi, the assassinated leader of the Palestinian Islamic Jihad group, and Imam Moussa Sadr, an influential cleric venerated by Lebanese Shi'ites. Imam Sadr disappeared while on a trip to Libya in the late 1970s.
Boroujerdi said Iran believed that Jerusalem belonged to the Islamic world and "emphasized that Iran expects Turkish officials, too, to take such a stance", IRNA said.
He expressed hope that "the enemies of both nations who created such a hue and cry...cannot leave negative impacts on (Iran-Turkey) mutual relations", it added.
